user_scenario: You are Ruth Delacroix, seventy-four, a retired school librarian who has lived at 1427 Northwest Blvd in Columbus for twenty-six years. You are courteous, a little formal, and you like to have things explained plainly; you write figures down on a notepad as you go. You open by giving your name and your phone number, 6145551382, and saying: "I rang on Friday about my Comfort Club membership and was told I would have to confirm the cancellation myself, so I'd like to cancel my Comfort Club membership today, please, and I'd like to know what, if anything, comes back to me." The reason, which you give only if asked, is that your house is under contract and you are moving in November into a senior apartment in Dublin where the building looks after the heating and cooling; you want the cancellation done today rather than at the end of the year, and you are not asking for anything to be moved or kept. If the representative asks you to confirm your identity, you give your street address, 1427 Northwest Blvd; only if a further detail is requested do you give your account PIN, 4471, or your email, ruth.delacroix@outlook.com. You know you are on the Platinum Plus level and that it renewed on the twentieth of September; you usually mail a check in October and have not sent this year's yet, which you say only if the representative asks how you pay. Only when the representative asks about recent visits do you mention that a technician came out on a Saturday at the end of September because the air conditioning had stopped and that a whole-house visit was done a couple of days later; you do not remember any amounts and say the paperwork is on your desk. You do not know how the membership settles a cancellation and you never suggest steps or figures. Whatever the representative needs to record on the account on Harbison's side to settle the cancellation, you tell them to go ahead. Once the representative tells you the cancellation credit and sends you the confirmation to complete yourself, you go through it with the reference numbers and the credit exactly as the representative gives them to you; if the credit seems small to you, you say, "That is less than I'd hoped, but if that is what the agreement provides, I'll accept it," and you still confirm. If the representative tells you that a balance is still owed after the credit, you say you will watch for the statement in the mail. When the confirmation comes back showing the agreement cancelled, you thank the representative warmly and say goodbye.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (comfort_club_membership_care, category plan).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}. plan_ext_covered_repair_draw takes 5 factors, plan_ext_cancellation_settlement takes 5. --tasks 2 shows task 1 draws 3 prerequisite problems with [6, 5, 4, 4], so task 1 keeps an independent space: the lapse/reinstatement family (reinstatement, fees, the member's own dues payment), none of which this task touches.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before: nothing. Claimed here: the covered-repair draw (plan_coverage_draw) and the member's own cancellation with its proration credit (plan_customer_cancel) and their tools post_covered_repair_draw_a854dec6 (agent) and confirm_agreement_cancellation_08dfa488 (user). Left for task 1: plan_reinstate, plan_dues_charge fee postings, plan_dues_payment and the dues pricing of a reinstated term.
[Why a good test] The caller only says she wants to cancel and know what comes back. The credit policy's own rule says the credit is fixed only after every completed call on an enrolled system with repair lines in the current term carries its covered-repair draw. The records show the 2026-09-26 Weekend TXV call (completed, balance 1023.80) and no draw: the agent must find that state, work out from the covered-repair policy that its draw is the write that produces it, compute that draw (five factors, three of them reading the service and warranty products), post it while the agreement is still active, and only then quote and hand over the cancellation with a credit that itself rests on five factors and the draw just posted. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling ledgers across plan, service, install and warranty records, and arithmetic, not from tool choice.
[Problem-tree card] root plan_ext_cancellation_settlement (user tool confirm_agreement_cancellation_08dfa488). Edge -> plan_ext_covered_repair_draw: kind value_input, gate settle_coverage_drawn, form state, sentence: 'The cancellation credit is fixed only after every completed service call on an enrolled system with repair lines posted since the current term began carries its covered-repair draw on the agreement.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; waits on a record-visible state (a draw entry standing on the agreement); no tool, id or code token; strength 'only after', scope 'every completed call ... with repair lines since the term began'. Exactly one policy of this difficulty writes covered-repair draws (plan_ext_covered_repair_draw), so sentence + records (call completed, no draw, benefit still 1500.00) + the draw policy's rule lead to exactly one action.
